curve_equation_G1: y^2 = x^3 + 4 over Fp; G1=<P0> of order r
curve_equation_G2: y^2 = x^3 + 4*(1+u) over Fp2; G2=<Q0> of order r
field_Fp12: Fp[w]/(w^12-2*w^6+2); coefficient list [c0,...,c11] means sum(ci*w^i); u maps to w^6-1
group_GT: Nonzero z in Fp12 with z^r=1; identity [1,0,...,0]

pairing.definition: e(P,Q)=py_ecc.optimized_bls12_381.pairing(Q,P,final_exponentiate=True) at the pinned commit; the library takes G2 first. P is supplied by the challenge and cannot be replaced. Raw Miller equality is not required.

challenge: Independently sample b uniformly from 1..r-1 and a uniformly from 0..r-1 by rejection sampling. Let P=[b]P0 and z=e(P,Q0)^a. Give only P and z, not a, b, [a]Q0 or sampling coins. P is uniform over nonidentity G1 and z is independently uniform over GT, including identity. Return Q in G2 such that e(P,Q)=z. No auxiliary powers are supplied.

input.P: Nonidentity G1 point fixed for this challenge instance

output.Q: G2 point satisfying e(P,Q)=z for the supplied P

acceptance: Decode P and z canonically; require P on the G1 curve, P!=infinity and [r]P=infinity, and require z!=0 and z^r=1. Decode the returned Q canonically; require Q on the G2 curve and [r]Q=infinity. Accept exactly when e(P,Q)=z, comparing all 12 coefficients. Q=infinity is valid exactly when z=1. Returning a scalar or substituting another P is not a solution.
encoding: UTF-8 JSON with exactly the stated input or output keys. Each Fp coefficient is 96 lowercase hex characters, no prefix, representing an integer less than p. A G1 point is {x,y} with Fp coefficients (input infinity is forbidden). A G2 point is null for infinity or {x,y} with each coordinate [c0,c1] in Fp2. A GT value is exactly 12 coefficients in increasing polynomial degree. Reject duplicate keys, noncanonical encodings, off-curve points and points outside the stated subgroups.
